holidays.name: Dance Like a Chicken Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to flapping your arms, bobbing your head, and strutting around like a chicken. Doing the Chicken Dance at weddings, parties, or in your kitchen is strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: The unofficial holiday is tied to the Chicken Dance, which came from a Swiss accordionist named Werner Thomas in the 1950s. The dance spread through Oktoberfest and wedding receptions worldwide.
holidays.funFact: The Chicken Dance is known in Germany as the Ententanz, which means Duck Dance, and it has been recorded in dozens of countries under different names.

holidays.name: National Buttermilk Biscuit Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the fluffy, flaky, buttery Southern staple. Bakers and breakfast lovers split open warm biscuits and top them with butter, jam, honey, or gravy.
holidays.origin: Biscuits have deep roots in American Southern cooking. Early versions came from British hard baked breads, and the use of buttermilk and baking soda or powder created the soft biscuit we know today. The food holiday is an unofficial observance.
holidays.funFact: The word biscuit comes from the Latin 'bis coctus,' meaning twice baked, even though a modern biscuit is baked only once.

holidays.name: International Hummus Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the creamy chickpea dip, with people dunking pita, carrots, and pretzels while arguing about the best toppings.
holidays.origin: Hummus is a Middle Eastern staple with a history stretching back centuries, and the day was created by hummus fans and food promoters to celebrate its popularity and nutrition.
holidays.funFact: The word hummus simply means chickpeas in Arabic, so asking for hummus is technically just asking for chickpeas.

holidays.name: Great American Pitch In Day
holidays.description: An observance for picking up litter and tidying up neighborhoods, parks, and streets. Volunteers grab gloves and trash bags to make a difference.
holidays.origin: The campaign was started by a national community cleanup movement to encourage civic pride and environmental responsibility, and it has been observed across the United States in spring.
holidays.funFact: The 'Pitch In' campaign has been credited with mobilizing millions of volunteers across communities to remove litter from public spaces.

holidays.name: Buy a Musical Instrument Day
holidays.description: A day that encourages you to finally buy that guitar, ukulele, or kazoo you always wanted. It is an excuse to start a new hobby and annoy your neighbors in the name of art.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created to encourage people to explore music and support musical instrument makers and local music shops.
holidays.funFact: Studies suggest that learning an instrument as an adult can boost memory and cognitive skills, so the kazoo might actually be good for your brain.
